card.name: Superlatives of scale and disaster
card.fires_on: The word that completes a superlative claim of magnitude, such as 'one of the great ecological disasters', 'the world's largest' or 'the biggest case'. It fires in news and web prose describing something as the greatest or most extreme of its kind.

modes.label: Disaster after 'greatest'
modes.description: A catastrophe noun completing a 'one of the greatest ...' phrase.
modes.example: leading to what may become one of the greatest environmental<< disasters>> in United States history.

modes.label: Largest or biggest
modes.description: The superlative adjective itself after 'the world's' or 'the'.
modes.example: one of the world's<< largest>> producers of gladiolus) in

modes.label: Noun after superlative
modes.description: A noun or adjective following 'most' or 'biggest' in a ranking claim.
modes.example: the most<< expensive>> and second-largest dam in the world.

card.writes: It suppresses words like 'major', 'big' and '重大', so it pushes the model away from 'major' wording after superlative framing.
card.plain: It marks the spot in a sentence where something is called the biggest or greatest of its kind, often a disaster.
